extracted.intended_audience: merchants, apprentices, and students learning commercial arithmetic and conversions
extracted.subtask_description: Practical arithmetic rules and procedures for merchants: computing profit and loss percentages, finding capital from a known gain or loss, handling repeated price changes, and reducing/converting between diverse coinage, weights, and measures by successive reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit percentage calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the percent gain when an item is bought at one price and sold at a higher price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the difference between selling price and cost, divide by the original cost (capital) and multiply by 100 to get percent gain. The text gives worked examples (e.g., buy at 100, sell at 112 produces 12% gain) and demonstrates the operations by multiplying and reducing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss percentage calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the percent loss when an item is sold for less than its cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the difference (cost minus selling price), divide by the original cost and multiply by 100 to obtain the percent loss. The manuscript shows multiple numeric examples and the corresponding multiplication/division steps to find the loss percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding capital from known gain percent and selling price
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a selling price and the percent gain made on the sale, find the original capital (cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat selling price as capital plus gain. To recover capital: multiply the known selling price by 100 and divide by (100 + gain%), or equivalently divide selling price into the proportion of capital to (capital+gain). The text provides step-by-step worked examples and warns about edge cases (e.g., when gain is limited or when multiple partial sales occur).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding selling price to achieve a desired gain percent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a capital (cost) and desired gain percent, compute the selling price that yields that gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiply the capital by (100 + desired_gain%) and then divide by 100. Examples in the text show this multiplication and reduction procedure and how to partition the resulting amount into currency denominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling repeated or partial sales (compound changes) for overall gain/loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute overall gain or loss when portions are sold at different prices or when price undergoes successive changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual shows how to treat each sale/price change by converting to capital+gain parts, multiplying through the sequence of operations (or reducing each part to a common basis) to accumulate net capital and gain. It gives examples multiplying successive rates and warns that some simple one-step rules may fail when gains are limited or when sales happen in parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating incidental costs into merchant calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for transport, duties, taxes, packaging, and other charges when computing real profit or loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common costs (transportation, gabella/tolls, stamping/marking, packing, charges for boats/ferries, port fees, barber/washer/other domestic expenses) and instructs to add these to cost before computing gain/loss, or include them as reductions from gross proceeds. Examples indicate adding such charges to total expense and reducing currency sums accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of multiple coinages to a common unit (successive reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce sums expressed in various local coins and denominations to a single common monetary unit by successive reductions through known denomination factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed stepwise: convert the less-frequent coins into the more-frequent/current local coin by multiplying/dividing by the denomination factors (examples include ducats, groats, picioli, etc.). The text supplies many numerical illustrations (e.g., reducing Venetian ducats to Rimini money) and prescribes the order and factors to use, while warning about choosing the proper target coin for the locale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of weights and measures between systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert quantities expressed in one system of weights/measures (grani, carati, quarti, ottavi, canne, braccia, etc.) to another system by successive partitioning and recombination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended method is hierarchical reduction: break a unit into its immediate subunits (e.g., grains to carats, carats to marcs) by repeated division/multiplication according to the standard factors; carry remainders appropriately; the text provides worked examples and tabulated reduction steps for many unit systems and materials (cloth, metals, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitioning sums into denomination parts (making change / 'partire in')
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide a money amount into parts according to denomination units to express it in higher/lower denominations or to make change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text prescribes 'partire in' procedures: successively partition the amount into units (e.g., into 12, into 4, into 100) following the denomination system; examples show converting a sum into ducats, groats, picioli, etc., by repeated partitioning and residual handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing multiple denominations simultaneously (aggregation and re-reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: When handling many different coins/measures together, aggregate and then reduce them to the chosen principal unit by repeated application of the same reduction rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate the different parts, then perform successive reductions to the principal unit (or to the unit demanded by the calculation). The text emphasizes being methodical (convert each part to the same intermediate unit first) and illustrates with examples combining several currencies and then reducing to one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and explanation of abbreviations and characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized abbreviations/characters for currencies, measures, and operations are listed and recommended for use in the manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a glossary of common abbreviations (e.g., S., p., g., b., car., grani, ecc.) and advises which abbreviations are useful to include for readers; recommends brevity and clarity, warns not to overload novices with too many obscure signs, and indicates where supplementary lists will appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of proportions and the rule of three
rubrics_metrics.description: Use proportional reasoning (including the rule of three) to relate quantities: prices, weights, measures, and money across different bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat proportional problems by forming the appropriate ratios and applying multiplication/division to find the unknown; the manuscript discusses composition and decomposition of proportions and gives many merchant-relevant instances (price per unit, scaling quantities, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stepwise algorithm for reducing coin/measure denominations (procedural recipe)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescriptive step-by-step method to reduce complex mixed-denomination amounts to desired unit by repeated local conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from the least frequent (largest) denomination or the most immediate subunit, then multiply/divide according to the fixed conversion factor to step down (or up). The text contains explicit step sequences and numeric examples showing each intermediate stage (e.g., how many carats in a marc, how many grains in a carat, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats and special cases where simple rules fail
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on circumstances in which the simple one-step rules do not apply (e.g., limited gains, partial sales, varying prices across lots), and how to adjust the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that rules assuming uniform percent gain may give incorrect results when gains are limited, when goods are sold in parts at different rates, or when denominational limits intervene; prescribes treating each part separately or using the more general compound-multiplication approach illustrated in the examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational advice for merchant records and computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations on how to organize calculations, choose a primary unit, and keep clear records when many measures and monies intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates selecting a convenient principal currency/measure for computations, reducing all items to that unit, using consistent abbreviations, and preparing tables of common conversions to speed work. The text emphasizes careful notation and practice so transactions involving many currencies/measures can be handled reliably.
